name: libforensic1394
desc: Live memory forensics over IEEE 1394 ("FireWire") interface
why: Reads live machine memory over FireWire DMA, a striking door into hardware-level memory access with a real huh.

brief.what_it_is: An open source C library, with Python bindings, for live memory forensics over the IEEE 1394 (FireWire) interface. It uses the direct memory access that FireWire offers to read a running machine's physical memory. The homepage says it runs on GNU/Linux and Mac OS X, and it exposes a simple C API for this. Its input is a 1394 connection to the target machine, and its output is the memory contents read over that link.
brief.why_it_exists: The author describes it as a modern alternative to pythonraw1394 (a Python wrapper around libraw1394), with native support for the newer "Juju" stack used by many GNU/Linux distributions. The homepage says it improves on existing libraries by offering a simple and clean interface to FireWire direct memory access.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage gives only a high-level account. The library presents an SBP-2 unit directory to a remote device so it can acquire physical memory access. It uses a vectorised API that exploits the asynchronous capabilities of 1394 controllers, and on Linux it works through the Juju stack, on Mac OS X through IOKit.
brief.install_notes: The homepage lists a git repository for the latest version and source tarballs for release 0.2 (libforensic1394-0.2.tar.gz and .zip). The build uses CMake and CPack. Hardware is implied to be a 1394 (FireWire) controller on the target and analysis side, but the homepage does not state requirements. Windows and FreeBSD are not supported. The homepage does not describe first-run steps or configuration.
brief.standout: It reads live physical memory through FireWire's DMA path, so the target machine needs no installed agent or software running on it. The page notes the author's own paper on the technique, which is the main source for the method.
brief.status: Quiet. The latest release, 0.2, was tagged 2010-10-05. A developer preview came out 2010-08-03. The page was last updated 2015-02-07, and the copyright line says 2015. The homepage describes the project as feature complete, with the Windows port postponed. I found no newer release or commit information on the page.
brief.caveats: Supported only on GNU/Linux and Mac OS X. FreeBSD and Windows support are listed as future work, and the Windows driver is described as requiring a prohibitively expensive cross-signing certificate. The known bugs and limitations are in a BUGS file in the source distribution, which I did not fetch. The release is from 2010 and the page was last updated in 2015, so current kernel and OS versions are untested as far as the page shows. The library is LGPLv3+. The Doxygen docs and the paper are referenced, but the page gives no direct URLs for them.
quotes: An open source (GNU LGPLv3+) library for performing live memory forensics over the IEEE 1394 ("FireWire") interface.
libforensic1394 improves upon existing libraries by providing a simple and clean interface to the the direct memory access functionality available over FireWire.
Available through git libforensic1394 is currently feature complete and undergoing extensive field testing.
